To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
common-sense cues are a powerful tool for improving transfer-learning for object detection.

(i) common-sense knowledge, acquired automatically from knowledge bases, can improve transfer-learning for object detection, and (ii), in particular, our approach can substantially improve the detection performance over existing state-of-the-art transfer-learning baselines on the challenging MS COCo dataset.

(a) we present a scalable approach that can be applied to any new category, (b) our method can transfer from one domain to another, and (c) we demonstrate that our method can transfer to categories that have never been seen before.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to transfer knowledge from source to target object categories in the context of detection.
the problem of detecting objects in new categories when training data with bounding box annotations are not available.
the problem of detecting objects in images when training data is only available for a subset of categories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method outperforms the state of the art by a significant margin, while requiring no additional human effort.
DOCK is a scalable approach for detecting objects by transferring Common-sence Knowledge from source to target.
DOCK outperforms all the existing state of the art transfer learning methods by a significant margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
common-sense can be a powerful tool for object detection.
common-sense can be used to improve the performance of object detection in a variety of scenarios.
we present a scalable approach to transfer knowledge from source to target category for detecting objects in images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
common-sense can be used to guide the transfer of knowledge from source to target domains.
common-sense can be used as a bridge to transfer knowledge from source to target classes, even when the training data for these target classes is very limited.
common-sense can be used to guide the transfer-learning process to improve detection performance.
